Welcome from Ms Helen Hayes, Headteacher
Welcome to Elmwood Infant School. We are a friendly and inclusive community where every child is valued and supported to thrive.
Our Staff and EthosOur staff are not only highly skilled but have been part of Elmwood for many years, bringing a wealth of experience and a deep understanding of how young children learn best. Their long-standing dedication shows how much they care about every child, creating a stable and nurturing environment where children feel safe, happy and ready to learn. We know how important friendships are, and we provide plenty of opportunities for children to make friends and feel part of our caring school community.
Our CurriculumElmwood’s goal is to give every child the strongest possible start. We prioritise learning to read, write and develop maths skills through lessons that are structured, engaging and enjoyable. Language development is key. Children build a rich vocabulary and learn to express themselves clearly and confidently, whether talking about their learning or engaging with friends. Alongside this, they enjoy a broad and balanced curriculum with opportunities for creativity, physical activity and exploration. We believe in developing the whole child, building confidence, curiosity and a love of learning that lasts a lifetime.
Our ValuesWe are proud to be a Gold Rights Respecting School, which means children’s rights shape our ethos and daily practice. For your child, this means learning in an environment where they are respected, listened to and encouraged to respect others, helping them grow into confident and caring individuals.
Come and See UsOur website offers lots of useful information, but nothing compares to seeing our school in action. We warmly invite you to visit and look around. We would love to welcome you and show you what makes Elmwood so special.
Warm regards,Helen HayesHeadteacher

Wraparound Care
Elmwood Infant School runs a Breakfast Club each morning in the school hall. The club operates from 7.30am to 8.40am, Monday to Friday, during term time only, and provides a calm, welcoming start to the school day.
Children enjoy a healthy, nutritious breakfast, followed by a range of quiet games and activities designed to help them settle happily before lessons begin. The club offers a smooth transition into the start of the school day, with staff on hand to support children as they move from Breakfast Club into their classrooms.
Children must arrive no later than 8.15am to ensure they have time to eat and take part in activities.
The cost is £5.50 per child, per day. All places must be booked and paid for via ParentPay by 6.00pm the previous evening. Please note that availability is limited to 25 spaces per day, so early booking is advised.
Breakfast Club is a great option for working parents and helps children start the day feeling settled, nourished and ready to learn.

Performance Data and Results
Understanding Our Results
Elmwood Infant School provides education for children aged 3 to 7, from Nursery to Year 2. As pupils transfer to a junior school at the end of Year 2, we do not receive or publish Key Stage 2 (KS2) results.
Instead, our published outcomes focus on the important early milestones achieved during a child's infant school education, including the Good Level of Development in Reception and the Phonics Screening Check. These measures demonstrate how well children are developing the knowledge and skills needed for future success.
Further Information
Parents and carers can view Elmwood Infant School's official performance information on the Department for Education's Compare School Performance website.
The website provides independent information about the school, including published attainment data, school characteristics and other key performance measures.
Please note that, as an infant school, Elmwood does not have Key Stage 2 results published on this website because pupils transfer to a junior school at the end of Year 2.

Rights Respecting School
Putting Children First
At Elmwood Infant School, children's rights are at the heart of everything we do. Every decision we make begins with one simple question:
"What is in the best interests of our children?"
We are proud to have achieved the UNICEF Gold Rights Respecting School Award, the highest level of recognition awarded by UNICEF UK. This recognises schools where children's rights are embedded throughout school life, creating a safe, inclusive and respectful environment where every child can flourish.
What This Means for Your Child
Children learn about the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) in age-appropriate ways throughout their time at Elmwood. They develop an understanding of their own rights, learn to respect the rights of others and discover how they can make a positive contribution to their school and the wider world.
Rights are woven through our curriculum, assemblies and wider school life. Throughout the year, children explore important themes through events such as Black History Month, Children's Mental Health Week, Anti-Bullying Week and charity initiatives. Each month, we also focus on a different Article of the Month, helping children understand how rights relate to everyday life.
Articles That Guide Our School
Article 3 The best interests of the child must be a top priority in all decisions and actions that affect children.
Article 29 Education should help every child develop their personality, talents and abilities to the fullest, while learning to respect human rights, other people, different cultures and the environment.
These principles reflect our vision of nurturing confident learners, building strong foundations and inspiring bright futures.
Being a Rights Respecting School is more than an award, it is part of our everyday life. It shapes our learning, our relationships and our commitment to ensuring every child feels safe, valued and able to thrive.

Welcome from our Chair of Governors
My name is Julie Hendry and I am the Chair of Governors.
We are very proud of our school and the special place that Elmwood Infant School and Nursery holds in our community. Through a combination of shared vision, a strong team and high expectations, Elmwood has consistently made progress towards becoming an exceptional school.
As Chair of Governors, I am pleased to have been involved in our development and the continuing success of our school. I am proud that Elmwood offers our children a place where they can feel safe and happy growing into confident young people by the time they leave us at the end of year two.
The governors are a group of committed and active volunteers, including parents who work in partnership with the headteacher and others on the senior leadership team to support school improvement.
We are all very proud of our school and recognise the hard work and commitment of the staff who work tirelessly to provide the very best opportunities for our children to succeed.
As governors, our role is to offer strategic guidance and to ensure that standards of teaching and learning are continuously and rigorously improved year upon year.
As a governing body, we also:
We have very high expectations and expect our children to make the best possible progress during their time with us and to prepare them for the future.
We welcome visitors to come and visit us to see the great things happening at Elmwood.

Curriculum
At Elmwood Infant School, we believe that every child has the right to a high-quality education that inspires curiosity, builds confidence and nurtures a lifelong love of learning. We are proud of our diverse school community and celebrate the different cultures, languages, experiences and backgrounds that make Elmwood a welcoming and inclusive place to learn.
Our curriculum is broad, balanced and ambitious. Rooted in the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework and the National Curriculum for Key Stage 1, it is carefully planned to ensure that all children develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to achieve their full potential. Learning is sequenced progressively, enabling children to build on prior knowledge, deepen their understanding and make meaningful connections as they move through the school.
As a UNICEF Rights Respecting Gold School, children's rights, wellbeing and personal development are at the heart of everything we do. Through our curriculum, children learn to understand their rights and responsibilities, value diversity, show kindness and respect towards others, and recognise the positive contribution they can make to their school, community and the wider world.
We have high expectations for every child and are committed to ensuring that all learners, including those with additional needs, have full access to a rich and rewarding curriculum. Learning is carefully planned so that children steadily develop their knowledge, skills and understanding across all subjects, enabling them to make strong progress from their individual starting points.
Reading, communication and language are central to our curriculum and provide the foundations for learning across all subjects. Through high-quality teaching, enriching experiences and an inclusive approach, we encourage children to develop confidence, resilience, independence and aspiration, helping them to become successful learners and responsible citizens.
We want our pupils to leave Elmwood as confident, compassionate and enthusiastic learners who are well prepared for the next stage of their education and equipped to make a positive contribution to society.
Our Early Years Foundation Stage provides children with a nurturing, stimulating and inspiring start to their school journey. We recognise that young children learn best through a combination of purposeful play, exploration, first-hand experiences and carefully planned teaching.
Learning in Nursery and Reception is organised through the seven areas of learning:
Our welcoming indoor and outdoor learning environments encourage curiosity, independence and creativity. Children are supported to explore, investigate, ask questions and develop a growing understanding of themselves and the world around them.
Strong relationships are at the heart of our Early Years provision. Staff know children well and carefully plan learning that builds upon their interests, needs and next steps. Through rich language experiences, storytelling, practical activities and play-based learning, children develop the foundations that will support their future success throughout school.
We value the important partnership between home and school and work closely with families to ensure every child feels happy, secure and ready to learn.
In Years 1 and 2, children follow a rich and engaging curriculum that develops both knowledge and skills across a broad range of subjects. Learning is carefully sequenced so that children build upon prior learning and deepen their understanding over time.
The curriculum includes:
Each subject is taught through a carefully sequenced curriculum that builds knowledge and skills progressively over time. Learning is planned to ensure that children develop a secure understanding of key concepts whilst remaining engaging, accessible and ambitious for all learners.
Underpinned by our Rights Respecting values, the curriculum helps children understand their rights and responsibilities, celebrate diversity, respect others and develop as active members of their community and the wider world. Through learning about different people, places, cultures and beliefs, children develop empathy, respect and an appreciation of the world around them.
Our commitment to children's wellbeing and personal development runs alongside academic achievement. Through PSHE, Relationships and Health Education, and wider enrichment opportunities, children develop the values, understanding and confidence needed to become kind, respectful and responsible citizens.
Physical development and healthy lifestyles are also a key part of our curriculum. Children benefit from high-quality Physical Education lessons, including specialist teaching from our sports coach, helping them to develop physical competence, teamwork, resilience and a lifelong enjoyment of being active.
Please explore the subject pages below to find out more about what children learn at Elmwood Infant School, how knowledge and skills progress across each year group, and how we support every child to achieve their very best.

Nursery
Nursery at Elmwood Infant School
Where curiosity is celebrated, friendships begin and children feel happy, safe and excited to learn.
A Welcome from the Headteacher
Choosing a Nursery is an important decision, and we’re delighted you’re considering Elmwood Infants. Our Nursery is a joyful, nurturing place where children feel safe, valued and excited to learn. We believe every child deserves the very best start, and our experienced Early Years team creates an environment full of curiosity, creativity and care.
We know how much trust families place in us. From the moment your child joins Elmwood, they become part of a community that celebrates their individuality, supports their wellbeing and helps them grow in confidence every single day. We look forward to welcoming you and your child into our school family.
Our Nursery Hours and Offer
From September, we are offering flexible part‑time options for families entitled to 15 hours, as well as full‑time places for those eligible for 30 hours.
Interested in Applying?
If you are interested in applying for a Nursery place at Elmwood Infant School, please come to the school office to collect an application form. Our office staff will be happy to help and answer any questions you may have.
Part‑Time (15 Hours)
Choose one of the following:
These longer blocks of time help children settle, build friendships, experience lunchtime routines and make stronger academic progress.
Full‑Time (30 Hours)
Families who are working or studying may be entitled to 30 hours of free childcare. We also offer the extended service to the end of the school day at no additional cost, giving families the option to use breakfast club and after school club if needed.
Nursery is where children learn to talk, listen, play, make friends, explore and become independent. It’s the foundation for everything that follows in Reception and beyond.
At Elmwood, we focus on:
Why Choose a School Nursery?
A smooth transition into Reception Children who start in our Nursery settle quickly into school life. They learn routines, build relationships with staff and feel secure in the environment they’ll move into for Reception.
Consistency and stability Your child experiences the same expectations, values and approaches they’ll meet throughout Elmwood Infants, supporting confidence and emotional wellbeing.
A strong sense of belonging Being part of the school community from the beginning helps children feel proud of their school and excited about learning.
What a Typical Day Looks Like
Children enjoy a balance of child‑led play and adult‑guided learning, including early phonics foundations, early maths, outdoor exploration, creative activities and story time. Our outdoor area is used every day, in all seasons, giving children space to climb, dig, build and explore nature.
Every child has a key person who gets to know them deeply, supports their wellbeing and keeps you updated on their progress.
Frequently Asked Questions
How old does my child need to be to join Nursery?
Children can join the term after they turn three.
Do you offer settling in sessions?
Yes. We work closely with families to ensure every child feels safe and confident. Settling in sessions are gentle, flexible and tailored to your child.
What should my child bring?
A named water bottle, a spare set of clothes and appropriate outdoor clothing. We go outside in all weathers.
Will my child have a key person?
Yes. Every child has a dedicated key person who builds a strong relationship with them and keeps you informed about their progress.
How do you support children with additional needs?
We are an inclusive school. Our experienced team works closely with families and external professionals to ensure every child receives the support they need to thrive. Please contact the SENDCo to discuss your child’s individual profile of strengths and additional needs.
How do you prepare children for Reception?
Through developing independence, confidence, early phonics and maths foundations, social skills and a love of learning. Children who attend our Nursery settle exceptionally well into Reception.
Can my child stay for breakfast club or after school club?
Yes. Our extended day offer means children can stay until the end of the school day at no additional cost, and families can choose to use breakfast club or after-school club if needed. Please be advised that there is a charge to attend breakfast and after-school club.

Pupil Premium
What is Pupil Premium? What is it’s purpose?
The Government believes that the Pupil Premium, which is additional to main school funding, is the best way to address the current underlying inequalities between children eligible for free school meals (FSM) and their peers by ensuring that funding to tackle disadvantage reaches the pupils who need it most.
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011 and is allocated to schools to work with pupils who have been registered for free school meals at any point in the last six years (known as ‘Ever 6 FSM’).
Schools also receive funding for children who have been looked after continuously for more than six months, and children of service personnel.
Accountability
The Government believes that head teachers and school leaders should decide how to use the Pupil Premium. They are held accountable for the decisions they make through:
